findings.detail: The first-setup path refuses to install without consent: sizeAndConfirm errors with "Confirm in an interactive terminal, or pass --yes" (head lines 275-278). The new already-set-up path in offer() uses `guard !confirmed, interactiveInput else` (line 203). That branch is entered when --yes is passed or when stdin is not a TTY, so a bare `darkbloom sandbox setup` from cron, ssh without a tty, or a script now reaches `install(...)` at line 191 and runs the full downloaded install.sh as the Mac owner without explicit approval. It does so when the installer's own `--plan` output reports a change that only adds slots. The decision comes from output of the remotely fetched script and from `SandboxSlotChange`, which is not in the supplied evidence. This widens the TB-013 / T-061 exposure to a run that previously only reported status. The installer can also update the add-on. Fix: when the input is non-interactive, apply only with explicit --yes and otherwise print the command. Alternatively, run only `--plan` and never `install` unless --yes.
findings.title: Already-set-up `sandbox setup` runs the downloaded installer without --yes whenever stdin is not a terminal

findings.detail: `SandboxTerminal.confirm` now takes `defaultYes`, and head line 463 returns true when `defaultYes && answer.isEmpty`. `readInput()` returns nil at EOF (Ctrl-D, closed or exhausted stdin), and `?? ""` turns that into an empty answer. With `defaultYes: true`, EOF therefore counts as approval, not just an Enter keypress. The new rerun prompt in `SandboxSetupTests` uses this default-yes path. That prompt can offer a plan that removes slots, and applying it runs the downloaded installer as the Mac owner (TB-013/T-061 surface). A closed stdin or a scripted pipe could silently apply the change, and a removal would be applied with no explicit `y`. Fix: treat a nil read as no, and apply the default only to an explicit empty line, for example `guard let line = readInput() else { return false }`. The flow that decides when the prompt is shown is not in the supplied evidence.
findings.title: Default-yes confirm treats EOF/closed stdin as consent to apply an installer slot change

findings.detail: SandboxTerminal.confirm now takes defaultYes. At head line 463 it returns true when defaultYes && answer.isEmpty. readInput() returns nil at EOF (Ctrl-D, closed stdin, exhausted pipe), and `?? ""` turns that into an empty answer, so EOF counts as approval instead of requiring a real Enter. The new already-set-up prompt (`Apply? [Y/n]`) uses this path. Per the docs, the prompt appears when the plan's counts differ from the installed ones, including plans that remove slots. Applying runs the freshly downloaded install.sh as the Mac owner and restarts the add-on (TB-013, T-061, A-019). A stray EOF, or a wrapper that has a pty but closes stdin early, can therefore apply a slot-removing change with no explicit answer. Fix: treat a nil read as no, for example `guard let line = readInput() else { return false }`, and apply the default only to an explicitly entered empty line.
findings.title: Default-yes confirm treats EOF/closed stdin as consent to a slot-changing installer run

findings.detail: Previously, rerunning `sandbox setup` on a set-up Mac only reported its status (base test expected the 'To change how many jobs run at a time' hint). Now the rerun downloads install.sh and runs it with `--plan`. When the plan only adds slots (SandboxSlotChange.onlyAdds, line 24), setup then runs the installer with `--yes` and the plan's counts. The rerunUnattended test shows this happens with confirmed=false and no terminal, so the owner gives no explicit consent. An interactive rerun also defaults to yes on an empty answer (confirm defaultYes, SandboxSetupProgress.swift:463). Trigger: any scripted or no-TTY rerun of setup, or the sandbox service (T-061 adversary) serving a plan with inflated counts. Result: a freshly downloaded installer runs as the Mac owner (TB-013, A-019) on a path that used to execute nothing. It also grows the VM capacity that competes with inference availability (A-018). The counts come from the installer and are only compared, never bounded. Fix: require `--yes` or an interactive confirmation before any unattended apply. Also record the rerun download/plan execution path in TB-013/T-061.
findings.title: Setup reruns now download and run the installer, and can apply slot additions without a prompt

findings.detail: The new default-yes prompt converts readInput() returning nil into an empty answer and therefore approves the change. On an interactive terminal, the owner can press Ctrl-D at the sizing prompt (or the terminal can lose its input) and setup will proceed with installation, including a plan that removes slots. This bypasses the new requirement that slot reductions receive interactive agreement; the noninteractive onlyAdds guard does not apply because interactiveInput was checked earlier. Preserve nil as a distinct result and return false on EOF, accepting the default only for an explicitly submitted empty line.
findings.title: End-of-input is treated as approval for slot changes
